flavor: A column of road crews will pay in coin for whatever the granary can spare — goads and bills, no haggling twice.
Cold-road traders weigh frostwood against a wagon of sawn stock and plate. They know what winter costs, and so do you.
Down from the Lantern Towns, two axles lost to the mud — Sarella says the timber must go before it warps, and the road forgets late payers.
Smoked and salted at Stillwater. Tomm Waterwise would rest the pond; the carter eats the profits otherwise, so the price stays honest.
Mine scrip spends poorly on an empty belly. The factor knows it, and prices accordingly.
Forge towns pay iron prices for straight beams. No questions, no receipts, no splinters.
Seed grain, cheap while the rows are green. Plant it or bake it — the price holds either way.
Timber week — every beam is spoken for twice over. Strike now or saw it yourself.
Cold stones, warm coin. The assayer pays over the odds when the mine breathes bright.
Bandages and broth for whoever needs them. The chapel takes its tithe in kindness, not coin.
